chapter: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
title: Trumbauer fronting, Ludwig and arrangement swaps with Fletcher
summary: Trumbauer stood in front while Ludwig still counted off; Blue Room and possibly Stampede went to Henderson, and he later arranged for Fletcher.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So How long after they got back to Detroit did they come out.

Oh, shortly after. It wasn't too long. Another thing that was done, that seemed to bug some of the guys, the [disc-ers] discos today, is while we were there, and as I say, we were short on arrangements, at least they figured we were, I guess -- maybe it was Ludwig, it could have been Horvath but very often he wasn't around all the time, but Ludwig had charge of the library and that part of the band.
Oh, did I mention that when we got to the Roseland, Trumbauer was standing up in front of the band.
As he was promised, and Ludwig is still beating off.
That didn't make for such a happy --

No, sir. That doesn't make sense anyway. Well, anyway, but Ludwig he really knew the tempo, he had been playing it for a long time. He had a lot to do with the band, and I'm just wondering what happened between him and Fletcher. They traded off a few new arrangements, so the first thing I know my Blue Room and a couple other things are being played by Fletcher, later, and we had a "Stampede," and

a couple of other things." Stampede" was supposed to have been recorded -- I just got a letter not long ago from Doc Reiker Ryker who has been bugged by some writer and he said, "You were there on the date, but ~~ and he said that you made Stampede, and I get credit for the arrangement. ^ Which You know, I didn't do ^ an's of course -- I am pretty sure I think it's Redmond's composition.

So I wrote back and told him, "Forget about things like that." The guy told him they had made it and I wasn't there at the recording so maybe they did n't make it; but some young kid tells me now that they made it but and it was rejected, so I don't know anything about it. But I think we had a couple other things too that were switched around between the bands.
That was They were a mutual admiration society. ^ We Got along very well with the Fletcher band.
Then they did "Singing the Blues" and I guess they did Bix's chorus.
Oh, yeah, I think I made that arrangement for them. Later on. I worked for Fletcher later on. I made arrangements for him and I made him a lot of things. I did some things of his.
How long were you in New York this first time?
